summary: Mentone sits pressed right against the base of the San Bernardino Mountains, where the Mill Creek canyon spills out onto the valley floor — and that geography defines everything about life here. The setting delivers dramatic vertical relief: the San Bernardino National Forest rises immediately to the east and south, putting serious trailheads within a short drive, while the view westward stretches across the Inland Empire's broad basin toward distant ridgelines. At just over 9,400 people spread across six square miles, the density is low enough to feel semi-rural in stretches, with pockets of properties backing up against scrubby foothill terrain rather than neighboring subdivisions. The home-value-to-income ratio sits around 5.9, notably more accessible than coastal Southern California, though a median household earning $70,466 would still face a tight monthly squeeze on a purchase. This is firmly a bedroom community — most employment draws from the healthcare, logistics, and public-sector jobs concentrated in nearby San Bernardino and Redlands, meaning daily commutes westward on CA-38 or I-10 are the norm. With an average 9.8 hours of sunshine daily and highs averaging 74°F, the climate rewards outdoor time, but summer heat can be punishing at the valley's edge. Mentone's essential tension is proximity without arrival: the mountains are right there, Redlands' downtown is minutes away, yet the community itself remains a pass-through corridor more than a destination.
